meta.description: Proposal-first scientific writing pipeline (installed as researchwrite) for research proposals, opening reports, research plans with evidence-grounded workflow. Three modes (compose/revise/hybrid), enforces evidence-before-prose, argument-before-sections, contracts-before-paragraphs. Four-layer QA pipeline (professor convener → avoid-ai-writing → auto-validation → scoring). Dynamic expert system (professor skill), foundation files (scope, research_canon, evidence_table, argument_map, section_contracts).

scientific_integrity.detail: Enforces evidence-before-prose (research_canon and evidence_table before drafting). Does not auto-upgrade facts (never changes 'may indicate' to 'proves' without evidence). Deletion preferred over explanation. Four-layer QA with professor expert review.

practice_boundaries.detail: Appropriate scope for proposal writing. Section contracts specify allowed/forbidden claims. Stopping rules for plateau, expert conflict, evidence gaps. Evidence-table maps claims to evidence. Argument-map before sections.

methodological_ground.detail: Evidence-before-prose, argument-before-sections, contracts-before-paragraphs principles sound. Professor dynamic expert dispatch by failure mode. QA pipeline order (content before language) correct. Eight-dimension scoring with four anchor points.

code_usability.detail: Project structure with foundation files (00_scope through 05_style_guide), state.json tracking, worked example (quaternary-proposal). Export scripts for .md/.docx. Validation checklist for claims/citations/numbering.

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive proposal writing: three modes (compose/revise/hybrid), foundation files (scope, canon, evidence, argument, contracts, style), four-layer QA (professor → anti-AI → validation → scoring), dynamic expert dispatch, reference numbering cascade, partial proposal scope, review framework. Minor: no explicit grant-specific templates (NSF, NIH, ERC).

reliability.note: Strong quality gates: evidence-before-prose enforced, section contracts (allowed/forbidden claims), auto-validation (claims have citations, methods reproducible, numbering continuous), four-layer QA, stopping rules (plateau, conflict, evidence gap). Minor: no validation that evidence_table covers all claims in draft.

performance_context.note: Efficient progressive loading: only mode-specific references loaded, professor dynamic dispatch. State.json tracks progress. Minor: no guidance for very long proposals (PhD thesis, 200+ pages), multi-agent parallel section writing mentioned but not detailed.

agent_usability.note: Clear nine-principle foundation. Mode dispatch clear. Project structure explicit. QA pipeline order (Gate 2 before Gate 1: content before language). Minor: worked example only for materials science (quaternary proposal), lacks examples for other fields. Professor dispatch by failure mode documented but integration with main workflow not explicit.

human_usability.note: Strong bilingual support (Chinese proposals, anti-slop for Chinese templates, Chinese review writing style). QA gear system (paper/proposal/internal/quick). Clear deliverables. Minor: steep learning curve with foundation files, compatibility trigger name (researchwrite) may confuse users expecting nature-proposal-writer.

security.note: Does not auto-upgrade facts, deletion over explanation. Section contracts prevent forbidden claims. Stopping rules prevent forcing completion. State.json tracks technical_debts. No credential handling.

maintainability.note: Excellent modular design: foundation files, mode-specific references (18 files), templates, state.json. Worked example for materials science. Clear extension points. Version tracking in state.json. Manifest-driven template/reference loading.

agent_specific.note: Strong evidence-grounding: research_canon, evidence_table, argument_map. Dynamic expert system (professor). Four-layer QA pipeline. State machine with state.json. Minor: no explicit token budget management for multi-round revision. Professor integration not seamless (requires separate skill). Parallel section writing mentioned but not operationalized.

key_strengths: Strong evidence-grounding principles: evidence-before-prose, argument-before-sections, contracts-before-paragraphs enforced via foundation files
Sophisticated QA pipeline: four layers (professor expert → anti-AI → auto-validation → scoring) with correct order (content before language)
Dynamic expert system: professor skill dispatch by failure mode, field-specific domain experts
Robust stopping rules: plateau, expert conflict, evidence gaps trigger stop (not force completion or fabricate evidence)
Comprehensive project structure: foundation files (scope, canon, evidence, argument, contracts, style), state.json tracking, worked example

recommendations.title: Add evidence-table coverage validation in auto-validation gate
recommendations.problem: Auto-validation (Gate 3) checks claims have citations and methods reproducible but doesn't validate that evidence_table covers all claims in draft. Claims can slip through if added during revision without updating evidence_table.
recommendations.root_cause: Validation checklist focused on formatting (citations, numbering) not evidence grounding.
recommendations.fix: Add to validation-checklist.md: evidence_table_coverage check that: (1) extracts all claim statements from draft, (2) verifies each claim has entry in 02_evidence_table.md, (3) flags uncovered claims as ERROR. Include in Gate 3 before scoring.

recommendations.title: Add explicit round-count tracking and enforcement in state.json
recommendations.problem: QA pipeline mentions 'targeted revision max 3 rounds' but state.json tracks mode/round/scores/technical_debts without explicit round-count enforcement. No automatic stopping after 3 rounds.
recommendations.root_cause: State tracking present but round limit not enforced programmatically.
recommendations.fix: Add to state.json: revision_rounds: {current: N, limit: 3, gear: 'proposal'}, phase_tracking: {current: 'intro', completed: ['scope']}. Add scripts/check_state.py that enforces round limit, recommends escalation after limit. Update partial-proposal-scope.md to use phase_tracking.

recommendations.title: Add grant-specific templates (NSF, NIH, ERC)
recommendations.problem: Worked example only for materials science quaternary proposal. No grant-specific templates for NSF (Broader Impacts, Intellectual Merit), NIH (Specific Aims, Research Strategy), ERC (sections A-B).
recommendations.root_cause: Generic research proposal focus, not grant application focused.
recommendations.fix: Add templates/grants/{nsf,nih,erc}/ with: (1) section_contracts tailored to each grant format, (2) evaluation_rubric with grant-specific dimensions, (3) worked examples for each. Update manifest.yaml templates.on_demand routing. Document grant-mode detection trigger.
